key_insight: Adding few-layer hBN to CsPbBr3 thin films sharply improves heat dissipation without changing the perovskite’s morphology or optical behavior.
engineering_relevance: A transparent, thermally conductive 2D capping layer can make perovskite optoelectronic devices more stable under high optical or electrical loading.
method: Large-scale semidry transfer of few-layer hBN onto planar hot-pressed CsPbBr3 films
Microscopic and spectroscopic characterization to verify unchanged film quality and optics
Heat diffusion simulations to compare capped vs. uncapped thermal behavior
evidence_signal: The heterostructure shows a measured thermal conductivity of 3 W/(m·K), about 7× higher than bare CsPbBr3 films (0.45 W/(m·K)), and is less affected by laser-induced heating.
watch_item: Scalability and long-term interface reliability of the hBN/perovskite stack under real device operating conditions still need validation.
paper_title: Improved Heat Dissipation in CsPbBr${_3}$-hBN Heterostructures
